name: Noise level map
corpus: six real photographs from the scikit-image sample data (astronaut, coffee, chelsea, rocket, motorcycle_left, motorcycle_right), each manipulated at seeded random places; 60 cases per condition

detection.task: Does an area (square of 30% of the short side) have noise unlike the rest of the image?
detection.positives: 60 images, each altered two ways (see true_positive_rate_by_condition)
detection.negatives: the same 60 images untouched, as given and re-saved at JPEG 90
detection.detected_means: an outlined area covers at least 30% of the altered square, at the default ratios (below 0.2x or above 8x)

known_failure_modes: Noise varies naturally with focus (out-of-focus backgrounds are smoother), texture and the camera's tone curve; 2-3x differences are common in authentic photographs.
JPEG compression removes noise in flat areas first, so after low-quality saving flat areas look 'clean' and can be outlined.
Small areas (under about three windows across) and areas that were given matching noise after editing are not found.
Added noise of a strength similar to the camera's own is not distinguishable.
how_to_reproduce: python -m forensic.validation run --only phase4 --pristine <folder with those six images>
